question: Will SpaceX successfully catch a booster with its tower chopsticks before 2027?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is no catch; the last tower catches were V2 boosters on Flights 5, 7 and 8, and V3 Super Heavy failed its landing burn on Flights 12 and 13 (Flight 14 booster outcome not found; web tools failed this run). Space.com on Oct 14 says Flight 15 is expected within about a month and SpaceX plans a ship catch; Manifold prices a booster catch attempt on F15 at 85%, and Polymarket prices a successful F15 booster catch at 0.57 (~$4k volume, closes Jul 2027, no 2026 deadline: a near-miss contract). Decomposition: P(F15 launches by Dec 31) ~0.75 x P(booster catch planned) ~0.85 x P(success) ~0.62, giving ~0.40, plus ~0.03 from a Flight 16 path, giving ~0.44. Polymarket adjusted for the deadline is ~0.48-0.50; I sit slightly below it because of the V3 landing record and schedule slip.

- Prior research saved in the repo's journal (Aug 2026): V3 Super Heavy 'failed its landing burn twice in a row'. Flight 12 (V3 debut) lost its booster during the return/landing burn; Flight 13's booster had a landing failure / landing-engine anomaly. Neither was a tower catch attempt.
- Flight 14 (Booster 21 / Ship 41, Pad 2, first orbital-plan flight): B21 full-duration static fire Aug 28. Launch slipped from NET Sep 15 to ~Sep 28 (journal traces say Starship began V3 Starlink deployment ~Sep 28). Booster outcome: searched, not found.
- Musk (Aug 20-21 2026) deferred the first ship tower catch by 'a few months', moving it from Flight 14 to Flight 15. An FAA tiered environmental assessment for Starbase return-to-launch-site landing was pending as of late Aug (comment period closed Aug 3); whether it has been issued since: not found.
- Historical Super Heavy tower catches (V1/V2): Flight 5 (Oct 2024) caught on the first try; Flight 6 waved off to the ocean (tower sensor issue); Flights 7 and 8 caught; Flight 9 used a reflown booster with no catch; Flights 10 and 11 did ocean splashdown experiments. So 3 of 4 catch-intended flights ended in a catch.
- Recent gaps between flights: Flight 13 Jul 24 to Flight 14 ~Sep 28 is ~66 days. Starship NET dates have repeatedly slipped (F13 had scrubs; F14 went from late Aug to Sep 15 to ~Sep 28).
- Event windows of the same length: from the 2026 V3 flights found, roughly 1 Starship launch per ~2 months, i.e. 1-2 integrated flights per 2.5-month window.
- Status quo: no V3 booster has yet been caught or landed successfully on record (F14 unknown). A catch requires F15 to fly, a catch to be planned, a go-call during the flight, and the booster staying on the arms intact for 1 hour.
- Resolution: needs an Oct 15-Dec 31 2026 catch by the Starbase tower chopsticks during an integrated flight test (ship stacked on top); booster intact for at least 1 hour (minor damage OK; may be removed from the arms early). Resolves off the actual flight outcome, not market contracts.
- Event window: 2026-10-15 -> 2026-12-31 per the criteria; as of 2026-10-15T03:00Z ~0% elapsed (77 days remain).
- Markets exist on Polymarket (F15 booster catch; F15 ship catch) and Manifold (F15 booster catch attempt). These are Flight-15-specific contracts closing in 2027, so their terms differ from this question's 2026 deadline.
- Searched but could not find (web tools failing): Flight 14 booster outcome, a firm Flight 15 date or FAA license, an official statement on whether the Flight 15 booster will attempt a catch or splash down, and the condition of the Pad 2 chopsticks.
